reference: The independently installed system `more` command (required as `more` in parity cases), exercising the POSIX stream and operand contract. The loadable documentation also specifies byte-exact nonterminal copying and named-file headers; nonterminal headers are independently checked against the installed util-linux reference. Bash type/help builtins provide the metadata contracts; they do not invoke the loadable.
coverage: Nonterminal stdin and regular-file copying with NUL bytes, CRLF, and unterminated final records
Multiple operand headers and a filename beginning with a dash
Repeated redirected stdin calls and stdout ordering
Unavailable operands continue without fabricated headers; directory notices retain later file output.
Invalid page-size options fail with status 1 and do not poison a later invocation.
The documented dash-stdin extension has an independent byte-copy contract.
exclusions: Interactive page keys, search, resizing, and terminal restoration need a controlling PTY; one focused case is deferred for a future disposable VM runner.
Backward navigation and rendered wrapped-row accounting are outside the documented loadable scope.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Compare nonterminal pipe copying byte-for-byte, including an embedded NUL, CRLF, and an unterminated final record.
Check a named regular-file operand preserves NUL data and the exact unterminated tail on nonterminal output.
Check the system more reference's multiple-operand header ordering around distinct binary and unterminated file contents.
cases.script: printf 'A\000one\n' > first; printf 'B\r\ntwo' > second; more first second

cases.purpose: Check repeated calls with separately redirected stdin retain stream ownership and preserve surrounding stdout order.
cases.script: printf 'left\000' > left; printf 'right\nend' > right; printf 'pre:'; more < left; printf '|'; more < right; printf '|'; more < left; printf ':post\n'

cases.purpose: Check the conventional -- separator allows a relative input filename beginning with a dash.
Check valid -d and -n options do not truncate a complete nonterminal stream when no page prompts can be used.
Record the system reference's status and diagnostic for a missing named input, while ensuring no stdout is fabricated.
Check rejection of an unsupported long option, including the reference exit status and presence of a diagnostic.
Use Bash's type builtin to assert that more is registered as a builtin without invoking it.
Use Bash's help builtin to verify the documented purpose and synopsis without invoking the more operation.
cases.script: doc=$(help more); [[ $doc == *'Page through input (POSIX more).'* ]] && [[ $doc == *'more [-d] [-n LINES] [FILE...]'* ]] && printf 'help contract ok\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise interactive page boundaries, Enter/space navigation, -d prompt text, forward search, quit across operands, and terminal-state restoration.
cases.reason: Paging, line advance, short-file EOF and termios restoration are exercised. -d prompt text, search and multi-operand quit have no fixture.

cases.purpose: Establish independent installed-reference status, streams and continuation for ordinary private input.
cases.script: printf 'first\n' > first; printf 'last\n' > last; more missing first absent last

cases.purpose: Establish independent installed-reference status, streams and continuation for ordinary private input.
cases.script: mkdir folder; printf 'last\n' > last; more folder last

cases.purpose: Invalid and overflowing page sizes and a missing -n value each return 1; a subsequent valid attached page-size invocation emits the complete named file.
cases.script:
printf 'complete\n' > rows
for arg in invalid 2147483648; do
 rc=0; more -n "$arg" || rc=$?
 printf 'rows=%s status=%s\n' "$arg" "$rc"
done
rc=0; more -n || rc=$?
printf 'missing-value=%s\n' "$rc"
more -n2 rows

cases.purpose: The documented custom dash-stdin operand retains byte-exact nonterminal copying without a named-file header across repeated calls.
